fixes.explanation: Moses, Israel's leader (Exodus 3:10), is a big name, and it's a fair guess. But he's not in this verse at all. Jesus says, "If the world hates you, understand that it hated Me first." He's talking about Himself.

That's what He says. "If they persecuted Me, they will persecute you as well…" Jesus just lined it up straight, no sugar on top. He isn't springing it on them later, either. He's telling them up front.

True! Jesus says it right after the persecution line: "if they kept My word, they will keep yours as well." He doesn't leave the disciples with only the heavy half. He gives the other half too: if they kept His word, they will keep theirs.
Moses, Israel's leader (Exodus 3:10), is a name I see coming to mind. But Jesus doesn't name him here. He says, "Whoever hates Me hates My Father as well." The answer is His Father.

True. Jesus says, "And you also must testify, because you have been with Me from the beginning." Just before that, He says the Advocate will testify about Him. The disciples must testify too, and Jesus gives their time with Him as the reason.

It's true, baker. Jesus says, "And you also must testify, because you have been with Me from the beginning." Just before that, He says the Advocate will testify about Him. The disciples must testify too, and Jesus gives their time with Him as the reason.
That's it. Jesus says, "I have told you these things so that you will not fall away." That's the purpose He gives. The verse says it plainly.

I get the instinct, friend. When you hear the world will hate you, swinging back sounds natural. But Jesus says, "I have told you these things so that you will not fall away." Not falling away is the purpose He gives, and fighting back isn't part of it.

Hiding sounds sensible when hatred is on the way, friend. But that's not the reason He gives. Jesus says, "I have told you these things so that you will not fall away." Not falling away is His stated purpose, and hiding isn't part of it.
Rome is a name I see coming to mind, but it isn't in this verse. Jesus says anyone who kills them "…will think he is offering a service to God." That's what He says, and it's a heavy thing to hear.
Jesus says otherwise. His words are, "I did not tell you these things from the beginning, because I was with you." He's telling them now. So the line is false.
Yes, it's false. Jesus says, "I did not tell you these things from the beginning, because I was with you." He's saying it now. The text gives that reason, so I don't have to guess.
